prediction:
THOUGHT: A 40-year-old woman with a 3-week history of a painless, progressively enlarging, well-circumscribed 3 x 3 cm anterior neck swelling plus symptoms of thyrotoxicosis (sweaty palms/soles, insomnia, irritability, fatigue). The mass is non-tender, non-fluctuant and non-pulsatile, arguing against inflammatory (subacute) thyroiditis, infectious abscess, or vascular lesion. Normal temperature, absence of cervical lymphadenopathy, and a normal-to-mildly elevated ESR (20 mm/hr) make subacute (De Quervain) thyroiditis unlikely (which is typically painful with markedly raised ESR). Graves disease usually produces a diffuse, symmetric goiter and frequently ocular signs; the described focal, solitary nodule is less consistent with Graves. A solitary, non-tender thyroid nodule producing hyperthyroid symptoms is most consistent with an autonomously functioning (toxic) thyroid nodule — i.e., a toxic adenoma (Plummer disease). Further evaluation (TSH, free T4/T3, thyroid autoantibodies, thyroid ultrasound and radionuclide uptake scan, and possible FNA if ultrasound concerning features) would confirm autonomy and guide management, but the clinical picture best fits a toxic solitary thyroid adenoma.

DIAGNOSIS: Toxic solitary thyroid adenoma (autonomously functioning thyroid nodule).

judge_response:
ANALYSIS: The predicted diagnosis (toxic solitary thyroid adenoma) does not match the reference (silent/painless thyroiditis). Silent thyroiditis is a transient, painless inflammatory thyrotoxicosis usually with a diffusely tenderless gland and low radioactive iodine uptake, not a single autonomously functioning nodule with focal uptake. The histories differ in expected exam and imaging findings; thus the diagnoses are not equivalent.

VERDICT: INCORRECT
